Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

justify verb

clear oneself or another of blame

also justify oneself, justification, excuse oneself, defend (an action)

classical

Cic. Fam. 12.25.3: quod tē mihi dē Semprōniō pūrgās, accipiō excūsātiōnem (Lewis & Short)
Plaut. Am. 3.2.28: ut mē pūrgārem tibi (Lewis & Short)

pūrgō, pūrgāre, pūrgāvī, pūrgātum

verb, first conjugation, transitive; sē pūrgāre alicui

clear of blame, excuse, justify

The figurative sense of “clean”: to clear someone of a charge, sē alicui dē aliquā rē pūrgāre (Lewis & Short).

Other words

  • excūsō, excūsāre, excūsāvī, excūsātum — excuse; plead in excuse

    verb, first conjugation · also used · classical · Cic. Att. 15.28 (Lewis & Short)

    To excuse a person or a fault, or to plead something as one’s excuse: valētūdinem excūsāre (Liv. 6.22) (Lewis & Short).

  • dēfendō, dēfendere, dēfendī, dēfēnsum — defend, maintain (a course of action)

    verb, third conjugation · also used · classical

    Of speech, to argue for something, or to allege it in one’s defence (Lewis & Short).

Examples

  • quod tē mihi dē Semprōniō pūrgās, accipiō excūsātiōnem

    as for your justifying yourself to me about Sempronius, I accept the excuseCic. Fam. 12.25.3 (Lewis & Short)

See also excuse, protect.

SourcesLewis & Short: purgo · Lewis & Short: excuso · Lewis & Short: defendo
